title: Finite free sheaf monomorphisms give normalized K-flat cokernel resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Work with sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $m,n\geq0$ and let $P,Q$ be module sheaves equipped with isomorphisms $P\cong R^{\oplus m}$ and $Q\cong R^{\oplus n}$, where the powers denote finite direct sums of the regular module sheaf. Let $u:P\to Q$ be any monomorphism and let $T=\operatorname{coker}(u)$ with its specified cokernel projection $q:Q\to T$. Define the cochain complex $C_u$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] by $C_u^{-1}=P$, $C_u^0=Q$, $d^{-1}=u$, and zero terms and differentials elsewhere. Its augmentation $\epsilon:C_u\to T[0]$, with $\epsilon^0=q$ and all other components zero, is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Every term of $C_u$, $P[0]$ and $Q[0]$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and all three complexes are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. In particular this specified augmentation is a K-flat resolution of $T[0]$. Here $N[0]$ places a module sheaf $N$ in degree zero. Equivalently $C_u$ is canonically identified with $\operatorname{Cone}(u[0])$, with differential $+u$, and the augmentation is normalized by $Q[0]\to C_u\xrightarrow{\epsilon}T[0]=q[0]$. No scalar origin of $u$ or constant-coefficient origin of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), specialized to finite free two-term complexes and single-term complexes; the quotient augmentation cohomology criterion is Homology Tag 0115 (definition-quasi-isomorphism-cochain).

proof.text: Work in the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since $u$ is monic and $q$ is its cokernel, $0\to P\xrightarrow{u}Q\xrightarrow{q}T\to0$ is short exact: its middle exactness is $\operatorname{im}(u)=\ker(q)$ in an abelian category, and a cokernel projection is epic. Placing these three objects in degree zero gives a short exact sequence of complexes (the degree-zero sequence is the displayed sequence and all other degrees are zero). The prescribed $C_u$ satisfies $d^{i+1}d^i=0$ since two successive differentials cannot both be nonzero. Moreover $qu=0$, so the prescribed components define the chain map $\epsilon:C_u\to T[0]$ by [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].

source.place: Section 010V, cochain complexes; degree-zero short exact sequence

proof.text: The cone convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $\operatorname{Cone}(u[0])^i=Q[0]^i\oplus P[0]^{i+1}$ with differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_Q&u[0]\\0&-d_P\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus its only nonzero terms are $P$ in degree $-1$ and $Q$ in degree $0$, and its only possible nonzero differential is $+u$. The canonical identifications $0\oplus P\cong P$ and $Q\oplus0\cong Q$ therefore identify this cone with $C_u$ as a complex, and its unshifted-summand inclusion with the map $j:Q[0]\to C_u$ whose degree-zero component is $1_Q$.

Apply [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso] to the short exact sequence $P[0]\xrightarrow{u[0]}Q[0]\xrightarrow{q[0]}T[0]$ from step 1. It gives a quasi-isomorphism from the cone to $T[0]$, equal to $q[0]$ on the $Q[0]$ summand and zero on the shifted $P[0]$ summand. Under the component identifications in step 2 this is exactly $\epsilon$, not merely some augmentation. Hence $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], and $\epsilon\circ j=q[0]$ holds componentwise: its degree-zero component is $q\circ1_Q=q$ and all other components are zero.

The unit isomorphism for the sheaf tensor product in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] identifies $\mathcal G\otimes_R R$ naturally with $\mathcal G$ for every module sheaf $\mathcal G$. Tensoring with $R$ therefore identifies each exact sequence with itself. Consequently the regular module sheaf $R$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. This uses the sheaf tensor unit, not any claim that sections of every flat sheaf are flat.

Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat] to the constant families with value $R$ indexed by $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Step 4 supplies flatness of each summand, so $R^{\oplus m}$ and $R^{\oplus n}$ are flat. The specified isomorphisms with $P$ and $Q$ induce natural isomorphisms of their tensor functors; exactness, hence flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], follows for $P$ and $Q$. The same cited coproduct statement with empty index set proves that the zero module sheaf is flat. Thus every term of $C_u$, $P[0]$ and $Q[0]$ is flat, including their zero terms.

All three complexes vanish in degrees greater than $0$. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] separately to $C_u$, $P[0]$ and $Q[0]$, using their termwise flatness from step 5 and the common upper bound $0$. All three are K-flat for the given arbitrary ringed site. Together with the specific quasi-isomorphism $\epsilon$ from step 3, the definition [def-pc-kflat-complex] says precisely that $\epsilon:C_u\to T[0]$ is a K-flat resolution. No property of the cokernel beyond its cokernel universal property, and no scalar origin for $u$ or $R$, entered the argument.
